description: Je suis Hervé Aziz Adoum, passionné par les nouvelles technologies, l’intelligence artificielle et l’innovation. Je suis ingénieur électronicien. J'ai aussi des connaissances en systèmes de drones et analyse de données. Curieux et orienté solutions, je souhaite mettre mes compétences au service du projet ASTROCAIR. Je recherche des personnes motivées, créatives et complémentaires, notamment en IA, développement logiciel, data science et santé, pour construire ensemble une solution innovante.
summary:
What we developed:
We developed ASTROCAIR (featuring the ASTRO EDGE interface), an offline-first, autonomous medical monitoring system and AI copilot. It integrates a local SQLite database, personalized NASA OSDR (Omics, Science, and Data Repository) baselines, and real-time tracking of cardiovascular, thermal, SpO2, psychological (BHP), and musculoskeletal metrics (including bone mineral density and ARED exercise compliance).

How it addresses the challenge:
ASTROCAIR addresses the challenges of spaceflight communication delays and intermittent connectivity by operating 100% locally. An onboard AI agent continuously evaluates live astronaut telemetry against individual OSDR baselines. When deviations or risks are detected, the system immediately generates clear, actionable "Conduite à tenir" (action protocols) and emergency guides, supported by a bidirectional Earth-shuttle synchronization center.

Why it is important:
Long-duration space missions demand absolute crew autonomy and real-time medical safety. By preventing microgravity hazards like accelerated bone demineralization and mitigating physiological or psychological distress without relying on constant ground support, ASTROCAIR safeguards astronaut health, ensures operational readiness, and guarantees mission success.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

  • What it does: ASTROCAIR (featuring the ASTRO EDGE interface) is an autonomous medical monitoring system and AI copilot designed for long-duration human spaceflight. It provides comprehensive biometric and musculoskeletal tracking for astronauts.
  • How it works: It is built on a 100% offline-first architecture that integrates a local SQLite database with personalized baselines from the NASA OSDR (Open Science Data Repository). An onboard AI agent continuously analyzes live telemetry streams (heart rate, core temperature, SpO2SpO_2SpO2​, psychological stress/BHP, bone loss rate, and ARED resistive exercise compliance) to detect anomalies against each astronaut's individual baseline. When risks or deviations arise, the system immediately generates emergency protocols and clear, actionable "Conduite à tenir" (actionable directives). A bidirectional synchronization center securely exchanges mission logs and updated baselines with Earth's Mission Control whenever a communication window opens.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Complete Operational Autonomy: Enables the crew to make critical medical decisions in real time, even during total signal blackouts or deep-space communication delays.
  • Proactive Medical Prevention: Identifies physiological degradation caused by microgravity (such as muscle atrophy and bone demineralization) early, preventing minor deviations from escalating into medical emergencies.
  • Intuitive Space Ergonomics: Delivers a clean, high-contrast visual interface (live telemetry overlaid against OSDR reference ranges, color-coded risk badges) that minimizes cognitive load during high-stress situations.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Safeguard Crew Health and Safety: Protects astronauts during deep-space exploration missions (such as lunar bases or Mars transit).
  • Ensure Mission Success: Maintains peak physical and cognitive crew readiness throughout extended deployments.
  • Advance Terrestrial Healthcare: Provides a resilient, autonomous tele-monitoring framework that can be adapted for extreme or isolated environments on Earth (remote clinics, polar expeditions, desert operations, or disaster zones without connectivity).

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages & Frameworks: Python for the AI agent logic and backend data processing; Streamlit for building the interactive user interface (ASTRO EDGE).
  • Data Visualization & Computation: Plotly for interactive telemetry vs. baseline graphs and gauges; NumPy for time-series modeling and mathematical processing.
  • Local Persistence: SQLite for the lightweight, embedded relational database onboard.
  • Scientific Standards: NASA-STD-3001 (Space Flight Human-System Standard) and NASA OSDR physiological baselines.
  • Version Control & Deployment: Git and GitHub for source code management and deployment readiness.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Intelligent Offline-First Paradigm: Unlike conventional health apps that rely on cloud processing, ASTROCAIR treats total disconnection as its baseline operating state, turning the spacecraft into a self-reliant medical hub.
  • Holistic Countermeasure Integration: Rather than monitoring vital signs in isolation, it bridges immediate acute care (cardiovascular/respiratory alerts) with long-term microgravity countermeasures (bone mineral density tracking and daily ARED workout compliance).
  • Immersive "ASTRO EDGE" Design: Features a purpose-built, mission-control visual aesthetic designed for rapid situational awareness and immediate readability.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Communication Latency and Blackouts: Engineered a resilient bidirectional sync queue to guarantee zero data loss during orbital shadows or deep-space signal delays.
  • Aerospace Medical Rigor: Strictly aligned alert thresholds and countermeasure logic with established NASA human-system standards and OSDR datasets.
  • User Cognitive Load Under Stress: Designed the AI outputs to be concise, directive, and immediately actionable so astronauts can execute emergency protocols without wading through raw medical data.
